title: Hospitality Customization Glossary
intro: Plain definitions of the terms that come up when a hotel, resort, club, or spa commissions custom branded guest goods. Each entry is written to be quoted: what the term means, why it matters, and where it appears in the HL Supply catalog.

terms.definition: The smallest quantity a product can be produced in. At HL Supply the MOQ is the first of four quantity tiers: 100 units for hats and leather goods, 200 for bags, bottles, and flip-flops, 1,000 pairs for slippers, and 100 to 250 for accessories depending on the item. Minimums exist because color matching, embroidery set-up, and tooling are fixed costs that only make sense across a run.

A price break reached at a set quantity. Every HL Supply product carries four tiers (for example 200, 500, 1,000, and 2,500 units); the unit price applies to the highest tier the order qualifies for, so an order of 999 units is priced at the 500 tier. Pricing is confirmed by the atelier at quote review.

A preliminary quote document generated from the quote cart once project details are complete, carrying an HLQ- reference. It lists selections, quantities, and active tiers so a buyer can circulate it internally before submitting to the concierge. Final pricing is confirmed after artwork and production review.

The identifier assigned to a quote cart submission, formatted HLQ-YYYY-NNNN. Quote the reference in any email to the concierge and the team can retrieve the selections, project details, and artwork attached to it.
The identifier assigned to a bespoke or mockup request, formatted HLB-YYYY-NNNN. It tracks a custom development or product adaptation through mockups, proofing, and quotation.

The approved specification a production run is made to: artwork placement and size, thread or etch colors, material, dimensions, and packaging. HL Supply production time (4 to 6 weeks) is counted from proof approval, which is why artwork readiness is the biggest lever on a delivery date.

A visual rendering of a product with the property's logo, colors, and placement applied, prepared before a proof. Mockups let a buyer share a direction with ownership or a brand team; they can be requested from any product page with a logo file.

Logo application by stitching thread directly into fabric. It is the standard finish for HL Supply bags, hats, slippers, and the sleep mask: durable, dimensional, and premium in hand. Artwork is digitized into a stitch file; fine detail and tiny lettering are simplified for stitch legibility.
Embroidery stitched in a thread color close to the fabric color, so the logo reads through texture rather than contrast. A frequent choice for suites and spas where a quieter mark suits the setting.

A logo pressed down into a material surface, leaving a recessed impression. It is the standard finish for HL Supply leather goods (trays, tags, boxes) and suits restrained branding; a blind deboss uses no ink or foil at all.
The opposite of a deboss: the logo is raised above the surface. Embossing is sometimes explored for bespoke leather pieces where a raised crest suits the design; the catalog finish is debossed.

A logo engraved into a hard surface by laser, removing or marking the top layer without ink. HL Supply uses it on bottles, sunglasses, umbrella handles, lens cloths, and yoga mats. The mark is permanent and does not chip, peel, or wash off.

A logo or pattern printed onto a surface rather than stitched or engraved. In the catalog it appears on flip-flop footbeds and straps, including all-over prints on the canvas style, where full-color artwork and repeating patterns are possible.
A flip-flop outsole molded with a reversed logo so that every step leaves the property's mark in the sand. A custom mold is tooled for the artwork, which is why this option carries extra set-up time.

Specifying a color by its Pantone Matching System reference so fabric, thread, foam, or coating can be matched to a property's brand palette. Share Pantone references with artwork; the proof confirms the match on the actual material.

Production in a color chosen by the property rather than a stock shade. Every HL Supply catalog product is offered in any custom color; striped and trimmed styles accept custom color pairings or combinations.
Where the mark sits on the product: front, side, or back on a cap; centered or offset on a tote; vamp on a slipper; handle on an umbrella. Placement is chosen at mockup and locked on the proof.

Logo files built from mathematical paths (AI, EPS, SVG, or vector PDF) rather than pixels. Vector artwork scales cleanly for digitizing, etching, and molds, so it is the preferred format at quote and mockup submission; PNG or JPG files are accepted but may need redrawing.

Converting a logo into a stitch file that tells an embroidery machine where each stitch goes. Good digitizing is the difference between a crisp crest and a blurry one, and it is why embroidered artwork is proofed before production.

The time between an approved proof and finished goods. HL Supply catalog products run 4 to 6 weeks after proof approval, plus transit to the destination; bespoke developments add design and sampling time confirmed in the proposal.

Made to a property's specification rather than chosen from stock. At HL Supply it covers two paths: adapting a catalog piece (dimensions, materials, colors, trims, hardware, packaging, logo method) or developing an entirely new product from a sketch, reference, or guest moment.

A product produced for and branded as the property's own, with no supplier branding, typically for a hotel boutique or retail collection. Woven labels, hangtags, and packaging can carry the property's identity end to end.

An item provided to guests as part of the stay rather than sold: slippers in the suite, a sleep mask on the pillow, flip-flops at the spa, a bottle at turndown. Amenity programs are planned property-wide, which is why slippers carry a 1,000-pair minimum.

Branded goods offered for sale in a hotel boutique or pro shop so guests can take the property home. Totes, caps, bottles, and sunglasses are the usual anchors; margins and sell-through improve when pieces are designed as objects guests genuinely want rather than souvenirs.

A branded item presented at check-in or placed in the room before arrival. Mini totes, luggage tags, and bottles are common; the best arrival gifts are useful during the stay and worth packing afterwards.

The evening service that prepares a room for the night. Slippers, a sleep mask, and a bottle of water are classic turndown placements, and a coordinated set in the property's colors turns the ritual into a signature.

An elevated gift for owners' guests, suite bookings, or event hosts. Leather goods, a woven tote, or a coordinated suite set are typical; quantities are smaller, which is where the 100-unit minimums on leather goods and hats help.
A plain-weave, densely woven cotton fabric prized for durability and a natural, resort-appropriate hand. It is the body material of most HL Supply totes and takes embroidery and custom dyeing well.
Canvas with enough weight or an internal stiffener to hold a squared, architectural shape when empty. The Pavilion Squared Tote uses it for a modern silhouette that stands on its own.

A synthetic leather alternative made without animal hide, chosen for consistent color, moisture resistance, and clean debossing. HL Supply leather goods use premium vegan leather with hand-finished edges; the Atelier tote uses a hand-woven version.
Leather made from animal hide. In the catalog it appears as the straps on the Sovereign tote, where a natural leather handle adds weight and patina to a canvas body.

A bottle construction with a vacuum between inner and outer walls that slows heat transfer, keeping drinks cold or hot for hours. HL Supply bottles use triple-wall vacuum-insulated stainless steel in 350 ml or 500 ml.
A food-grade, corrosion-resistant steel alloy used for drinkware. The Aura bottle is built from it; the material does not retain flavors and is safe for daily use in suites and spas.
A looped cotton pile fabric, the same family as a hotel towel, chosen for softness and absorbency. The Cloud slipper uses plush terry cotton fleece for the classic spa feel.
A textured cotton weave with a raised grid pattern that is lighter and more breathable than terry. The Lattice slipper uses it for warm-climate properties and poolside use.

A closed-cell foam compound used for flip-flop soles and footbeds; density controls cushioning and durability. The Essential is produced in a 100% recyclable grade and the Impression in a high-rebound grade for its molded outsole.

Sunglass lenses with a filter that cuts glare reflected from water, sand, and pavement, in addition to UV protection. The Pilot aviator carries polarized UV lenses, suited to pool decks and coastlines.

A plant-derived plastic used for quality sunglass frames because it holds rich color, takes a matte or gloss finish, and is comfortable against skin. The Icon and Avant sunglasses use acetate frames with laser-etched logos.
A finely woven synthetic cloth that lifts oils and dust without scratching lenses or screens. The Clarity lens cloth is a lint-free microfiber square with a laser-etched logo and a travel pouch.

A cap with buckram or interfacing in the front panels so the crown holds its shape without a head inside. Structured caps (the Regent, the Fairway, the Summit's front crown) present a logo crisply and read as polished.
A cap without stiffening in the crown, so it sits low and soft. The Heritage dad hat is unstructured washed twill, giving a relaxed, lived-in look that suits leisure retail.
The classic baseball cap construction made from six triangular panels meeting at a top button. The front two panels carry the embroidery; the Regent Classic Cap is a reinforced six-panel.

A cap with a structured foam or fabric front and breathable mesh back panels, closed with an adjustable snap. The Summit uses a cotton front with mesh backing, popular for marinas, mountain properties, and outdoor events.
A soft hat with a downward-sloping brim all the way around for full sun protection. The Riviera is premium cotton twill with a relaxed crown, the beach-club and poolside staple of the collection.
Presentation packaging beyond the standard individual wrap: boxes, pouches, tissue, ribbons, and cards in the property's identity. Available on every catalog product and quoted alongside the goods.

Splitting a large order into scheduled shipments so a property receives amenity stock as it is needed rather than all at once. Common for slipper and flip-flop programs; note the preference in the quote.

The catalog code printed on every product page and specification table (B-001 for the Signature Solid Tote, H-005 for the Fairway Golf Cap, and so on). Quote it in emails and purchase orders to avoid ambiguity between similar styles.

A property's set of branded pieces for guests who travel with a dog: typically a bowl and toy placed in the room before arrival, a bandana as the take-home, and a lead, travel bowl, and waste-bag pouch sold at the boutique or added to a VIP arrival kit. HL Supply's Pet Collection is one-size by design and excludes beds, collars, and clothing.

A small fabric label with the logo woven into the threads rather than printed on top, sewn onto a textile piece. Used on the Harbor Rope Toy and available as a bespoke detail on bags and slippers; it reads as a maker's mark and survives washing.

A dry, baked color coating on metal that gives stainless steel a matte, durable surface in any custom color. On the Companion Bowl and the bottle collection the logo is laser-etched through the coating, so the mark is permanent and reads crisply against the color.

HL Supply's name for the team that receives quotes, bespoke requests, and messages, replies with product direction, and manages a project through proofing and delivery. Reach them from any page or at info@hotelluxurysupply.com.
